basis: Gastric mucosal injury is driven by intraepithelial T-cell inflammation; associated coeliac disease does not add organs.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: lymphocytic gastritis is an immune-mediated gastric mucosal disorder, rather than merely an association with coeliac disease.

basis: Defining skin, skeletal and gingival/dental disease; cognitive impairment 30-79%. Cap omits prolonged bleeding time (3/3) and high myopia (1/3), prioritizing neurodevelopmental impairment.

decisions.haematologic: none: prolonged bleeding time (3/3) supports involvement, but the four-axis cap prioritizes defining organs and more consequential neurodevelopmental impairment.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: gingival overgrowth (7/7) and abnormal dentition (80-99%) are characteristic components of the syndrome's definition.
decisions.neurologic: involved: cognitive impairment is frequent (30-79%), supporting direct neurodevelopmental dysfunction.

basis: Hereditary noncirrhotic portal vascular disease affects hepatic circulation; congestive splenic dysfunction with cytopenias occurs in >50% over the usual course.

decisions.haematologic: involved: congestive hypersplenism with cytopenias affects >50% in the usual course of noncirrhotic portal hypertension.
decisions.hepatic: primary: the hereditary subtypes are hepatic portal vascular disorders; absence of cirrhosis does not exclude hepatic disease.

basis: Stated Down syndrome subtype: neurodevelopmental disability; heart defects ~40-50%, hearing impairment ~50-75%, visual dysfunction >50%. Balanced wording makes subtype interpretation uncertain.

decisions.ocular: involved: intrinsic visual dysfunction, including significant refractive errors and strabismus, affects >50% in Down syndrome.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment affects ~50-75% in Down syndrome, including persistent conductive and sensorineural dysfunction.

basis: Anterior pituitary hormone deficiency defines the disorder. Intellectual disability is explicitly optional; its frequency is not established at >=30%.

decisions.neurologic: none: intellectual disability is explicitly present only in some cases; neither a required criterion nor a frequency >=30% is established for this umbrella.

basis: Named neurocardiorenal malformations define three axes; CNS disease is documented. Microdontia (2/2) alone does not establish oral functional injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: microdontia (2/2) is a minor structural finding without established functional damage; feeding difficulties alone do not demonstrate gastrointestinal injury.

basis: Destructive nasal/sinus lesion is predominantly NK/T-cell lymphoma, a blood-cell neoplasm. Palatal destruction is explicitly part of the defining lesion, qualifying without a frequency estimate.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the vast majority are malignant NK/T-cell lymphoproliferations, constituting a disease of blood cells even at an extranodal site.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: palatal destruction is part of the explicit disease definition; three primary slots are occupied by nasal origin and mandatory lymphoma mechanism axes.

basis: Defining skeletal, palatal and dental malformations; airway obstruction occurs in 30-79%; global developmental delay in 11/25 (44%) supports neurologic involvement beyond speech delay.

decisions.neurologic: involved: global developmental delay occurs in 11/25 (44%); this exceeds the threshold and is broader than speech impairment from craniofacial defects.

basis: Immune-mediated chronic photodermatosis; persistent cheilitis affects ~60-70% and chronic conjunctivitis ~30-50%, sometimes with scarring. Renal injury is not established as common.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: persistent inflammatory cheilitis affects ~60-70%, constituting chronic lip/oral mucosal disease.
decisions.ocular: involved: chronic conjunctival inflammation affects ~30-50% and may scar; this is persistent ocular disease rather than transient conjunctival injection.

basis: Vitreous inflammation defines ocular disease; this finding alone does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated cause.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: vitritis describes an inflammatory reaction with multiple possible causes; the concept does not establish infection or immune-mediated disease.
